materials.title: Coats at the school concert
materials.text:
Choose the best reply in each conversation.

1. Teacher: Please leave your coats on these hooks.
Child: ____

2. Child: Which row are our seats in?
Teacher: ____

3. Teacher: The show is starting. Please put your phone away.
Child: ____

4. Child: I cannot see over that tall hat.
Teacher: ____

5. Teacher: Did you enjoy the last song?
Child: ____

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Please leave your coats on these hooks.
Child: ____
options: All right. I will hang mine here.
questions.explanation: Hanging the coat follows the instruction. Family/object identification and counting do not.

questions.prompt:
Child: Which row are our seats in?
Teacher: ____
options: The third row, beside the window.
questions.explanation: Row and location identify seats. Scarf/ability/food preference do not.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: The show is starting. Please put your phone away.
Child: ____
options: Yes. I will put it in my bag.
questions.explanation: Putting the phone in the bag responds to the instruction. Animal/time/address information does not.

questions.prompt:
Child: I cannot see over that tall hat.
Teacher: ____
options: Let’s ask politely if the hat can come off.
questions.explanation: A polite request addresses the blocked view. Taste/family/train colour do not.

questions.prompt:
Teacher: Did you enjoy the last song?
Child: ____
options: Yes. The quiet ending was lovely.
questions.explanation: The opinion about the ending answers enjoyment. Location/pet count/time do not.

units.title: The bell at home
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The bell at home
materials.text:
Owen gets a new bell for his bicycle. It is silver and makes a clear ringing sound. He wants to try it in the garden, but his little sister is asleep in her room beside the garden.

Dad asks him to wait. Owen puts the bell on the kitchen table and draws a picture of his bike instead. He colours the frame red and the wheels black.

When his sister wakes up, she comes to look at the picture. Then they go outside with Dad. Owen rings the bell once. His sister laughs and rings her toy bell too. The two bells make very different sounds.

questions.prompt: Owen’s new bell is silver.
questions.explanation: Its colour is stated.

questions.prompt: His sister is awake at first.
questions.explanation: She is asleep when he first wants to ring it.

questions.prompt: Owen draws while he waits.
questions.explanation: He draws the bicycle instead.

questions.prompt: The bicycle frame in the picture is green.
questions.explanation: He colours the frame red.

questions.prompt: The two bells sound the same.
questions.explanation: The ending says their sounds are very different.

units.title: The red folder
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The red folder
materials.text:
Amira takes a red folder to her music lesson. It holds three pages of songs. On the bus, she puts it beside her on the seat. When she gets off, she remembers it just in time and picks it up.

At the music room, her teacher gives her a new page. "Put this behind the other songs," she says. Amira opens the folder, adds the page and closes it carefully.

At home, Mum asks which song she will practise first. Amira takes out the new one. It has a small picture of a boat at the top. She starts slowly, then sings it again with Mum.

questions.prompt: Amira carries a red folder.
questions.explanation: The folder is red.

questions.prompt: She leaves the folder on the bus.
questions.explanation: She remembers and picks it up before leaving.

questions.prompt: The teacher gives her one new page.
questions.explanation: One new song page is added.

questions.prompt: The new page has a picture of a car.
questions.explanation: The picture is a boat.

questions.prompt: Amira sings the new song with Mum.
questions.explanation: She repeats it with Mum at the end.

units.title: The little clay bird
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: The little clay bird
materials.text:
Theo makes a small bird from clay at school. Its body is round and its tail is short. He adds two little wings, then asks the teacher where it should dry.

The teacher shows him a shelf by the wall. Theo puts his name on a piece of paper beside the bird. He does not write on its wet body.

The next day, the teacher says the bird needs more time. Theo looks at it but leaves it on the shelf. On Friday, he can take it home. He puts it in a small box with soft paper around it. Grandma opens the box and smiles at the bird's funny feet.

questions.prompt: Theo makes the bird from clay.
questions.explanation: Clay is the material given.

questions.prompt: The bird has a long tail.
questions.explanation: Its tail is short.

questions.prompt: Theo writes his name on the wet bird.
questions.explanation: He writes on separate paper beside it.

questions.prompt: Theo takes it home the next day.
questions.explanation: He waits until Friday.

questions.prompt: Soft paper protects the bird in its box.
questions.explanation: It is packed with soft paper around it.

units.title: Two maps for the picnic
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: Two maps for the picnic
materials.text:
Ella draws a map from her house to the picnic field. She puts the shop on the left and the bridge near the top. Her brother Max draws a second map. His shop is on the right because he is looking from the other end of the road.

They show both maps to Dad. He asks them to add a starting point and arrows. Now it is easier to see which way each map goes.

At the field, they put the maps under a stone so the wind cannot take them. After lunch, Max follows Ella's arrows home. She follows his. Both children arrive at their front door together.

questions.prompt: Ella and Max each draw a map.
questions.explanation: There are two maps by the two children.

questions.prompt: The shop is on the same side in both drawings.
questions.explanation: It is left in one and right in the other.

questions.prompt: Dad asks them to add arrows.
questions.explanation: He asks for starting points and arrows.

questions.prompt: The children throw the maps into the river.
questions.explanation: They place them under a stone at the field.

questions.prompt: They both get home using each other’s map.
questions.explanation: Each follows the other’s arrows and reaches the front door.

units.title: A hat for the snowman
units.instruction: Read the whole story. Choose True or False for each sentence.

materials.title: A hat for the snowman
materials.text:
In this winter story, two children make a snowman in their garden. Jo brings a small carrot for its nose. Her brother Nick brings two dark stones for its eyes.

The snowman has no hat. Nick wants to use Dad's warm wool hat, but Dad needs it for his walk. Jo finds an old flowerpot in the shed. They brush it clean and turn it upside down on the snowman's head.

Dad laughs when he comes outside. "That is a very tall hat," he says. Before leaving, he takes a photo. The children stand beside their snowman, each wearing their own wool hat in the cold air.

questions.prompt: Jo brings a carrot for the nose.
questions.explanation: Jo supplies the carrot nose.

questions.prompt: Nick uses buttons for the eyes.
questions.explanation: He brings dark stones.

questions.prompt: Dad gives away the hat he needs for his walk.
questions.explanation: He keeps his warm hat; the snowman uses a pot.

questions.prompt: An old flowerpot becomes the snowman’s hat.
questions.explanation: It is cleaned and turned upside down on its head.

questions.prompt: The children wear their own hats outside.
questions.explanation: The final sentence states both are wearing their hats.
